column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. The curriculum addresses AI-assisted coding environments, agent skills, model context protocols, requirements engineering with executable specifications, automated testing, and software factory architectures. The course is taught through lectures, tutorials, and laboratory sessions emphasizing hands-on development and experimentation. Upon completion, students will be able to construct developer workflows incorporating AI-assisted coding tools, implement agent skills and context engineering mechanisms, translate informal requirements into executable specifications, evaluate reliability and performance of AI-generated code, and architect end-to-end agentic software development factories.

Course Code: Construct developer workflows incorporating AI-assisted coding tools and coding agents, for a given software development task, such that all public tests pass and no warnings from the configured static analyser.
column2: Implement agent skills, tool uses, and context engineering mechanisms, using an agent orchestration framework, justifying each design decision against at least one stated requirement.
column3: Translate informal system requirements into executable specifications and structured prompt specifications, for a supplied problem statement, covering every use case in the supplied requirements document.
column4: Evaluate the reliability and performance of AI-generated code and software development loops, using automated testing and evaluation metrics, identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence.
column5: Architect an end-to-end agentic software development factory, incorporating coding agents, iterative loops, and automated deployment pipelines, demonstrated live, with 3 scenario walkthroughs chosen by the evaluator.
